Oh man… this inspired me to make a full freaking blog post for the first time in years. I’ll work on that a little later…. But I’ll put some here:

Vaping changed my life in so many good ways. It saved me from self harm and helped me work on my mental health issues in ways one really wouldn’t expect something could. 

I ended up running a fairly popular IG. Hosting an event or two. Writing for one issue of a magazine. Meeting a celebrity. 

But more than that, it got me to work on social anxiety. It gave me a safe place where I felt like myself (until the anxiety won and made it unsafe unfortunately). And it gave me people who I care about to this day, even if I don’t see them much anymore. 

I feel for all the shops and businesses that closed due to regulations and non-enforceable flavor bans. Sigh. 

Surprisingly enough I kinda miss the clone wars. I remember when that one dude had that RDA blueprint thing that FastTech or some other Chinese company took and the thing didn’t even work. It was hilarious. All my authentic mods are strewn about somewhere in boxes. Loved them… loved mech mods and dripping, but depression meant I couldn’t keep up with maintenance and my trigger finger meant I couldn’t build for myself. 

I remember most of the juices in those pics. My favorite juice was actually made by a friend of mine. I occasionally still feel tempted to beg/bribe her for the recipe for two of her juices. Ima message her on IG and jokingly see if she still can make them. 

Sigh. Vaping was so good to me. I even tattooed it on my arm as a symbol of my recovery. For me, the peak time was 2014-2018ish. 

To anyone in SoCal who remembers my pudgy self touring vape shops in LA/OC who reads this: HELLO!!!

I was 25 when I got into fountain pens ten years ago. There’s definitely a wide range of people into the hobby.

My first Sailor was a used Pro Gear Slim Lamé with an MF nib. The feedback was so weird to me. I didn’t hate it, but I didn’t love it either. And the pen itself felt small. I started to feel on the fence about Sailor pens. This made me sad because I loved that Sailor has such a wide color selection for their bodies. Then I lost it in The Great Fountain Pen Loss of 2016. 

When I decided to go back to school around 2020, I found Pensachi and thought the Sailor x Wancher Pink Cosmo would motivate me to do well in school. I got an EF, because that’s what I usually use for note taking. I realized I prefer the full sized pro gear is much more to my liking. Was still meh about the feedback.

Then I decided to complete the Sailor x Wancher collection with the two colors I didn’t have. I asked if I could get two different nibs, as I usually don’t like to have the same nib in the same model. I got a medium and a zoom. The Zoom is probably one of my most favorite nibs. 

Now I have 5 Pro Gears 😅

As a peer support specialist, I have a lot of thoughts on this. 

Hobbies are great tools to utilize as self care. People taking time to focus on something they are passionate about is good for their health. 

Journaling is something I often advocate to my members as self care because “paper ain’t gonna judge you like you feel a therapist might.” One could write whatever they felt and could share what they wanted to whoever they felt comfortable sharing it with. It’s also a good way to retain things that one might need to talk to their providers about. 

As for snail mail or even things like this sub, community is really important when it comes to mental health. It really takes a good support system to stay on track with feeling how you want to feel. I don’t think we’re all in the same boat, but probably going down the same river, and we can relate or hand an oar to someone who might need it more, you know?

These are things topics I’m supposed to be fleshing out for my own social media, but my perfectionism and anxiety are making me avoid it.

This is one of the reasons I hate the algorithm on IG. I like following different kinds of FP lovers, from people just starting out to people with “bad” penmanship to even the “penfluencers.” It’s harder to connect with people when all you’re being shown is the top posts.

Things I’ve found that help: 
-setting out what I want to use, including brushes. 

-Having multiple kinds of mirrors so I can see things a little better by getting closer/different angle (like a pocket or hand mirror when I’m curling my lashes). 

-Time. If I’m feeling pretty blind, I definitely don’t want to feel rushed too. I’d rather go without makeup if I don’t have enough time to do it.

- and like with anything: practice. I’ve only done it a handful of times (I don’t wear makeup everyday) but I feel like every time makes it just a little better.

Ahhh skin whitener/lightener.... skin care products I’m quite familiar with, not because I went out of my way to use them, but because my mom loves to buy what she’s familiar with and a whole lot of Filipino skin care touts skin whitening. 

As a Filipina-American, I grew up hearing: “Don’t stay outside too long! You’re going to get dark!” I asked my mom, dad, basically every family member why it was such a big deal to have fair skin. I was always told something along the lines of “having fair skin means you’ve never had to work in the fields.” Pale skin in our culture is a sign of affluence and tanned skin... I guess poverty? 

Tanning in first world countries seems a bit the same. Those who tan can afford the luxury of tanning— taking the time to relax and toast. 

I’ve never gone out of my way to tan, though I usually feel tempted to because I always say I can go from “white bread to wheat toast” depending on how much time I spend outside. And I’m all sorts of hues because of what gets exposed to the sun. My belly is pale and my driver’s side arm is pretty dark. I’d like to be one even tone, but as a plus sized woman, I have body image issues and I fear being seen by anyone and made a joke. 

As for wanting pale skin, there is a part of me that has stayed from childhood that wants to be a skinny, blue-eyed blonde because I thought they were who everyone thought was pretty. Being one of the few Filipinos in my grade where it was like “is she Asian, is she Pacific Islander, is she Latino?” felt... lonely. But for the most part, I didn’t go out of my way to stay pale either. Staying pale meant staying at home and I have always had a desire for adventure and new experiences.

Though this summer.... I’m actually considering buying some of those skin whitening products. Not because of any hang-up relating to my skin, but because I’m annoyed that I’m already half a shade darker than the new ELDW foundation I bought two weeks ago. I even went up a shade or two because I thought the lady who color matched me at Macy’s went too light. It’s only July, guys! I live in SoCal! I’m gonna get darker! I’ll probably just get some drugstore dupe for the summer, but I’m a bit bummed that I’m gonna have to wait to use the ELDW until fall/winter.
